name: Task Prioritization
description: Three-phase AI pipeline: semantic analysis → constraint analysis → ranked synthesis. Reads all Task nodes and [:BLOCKS] relationships from Neo4j, ranks them, and returns finalRank + reasoning per task.

nodes.label: Neo4j — Fetch All Tasks

config.neo4jdb.db_description: Task graph. Nodes are (:Task {id, title, createdAt, priority}). Relationships are [:BLOCKS] from a blocker task to a blocked task.

nodes.query: MATCH (t:Task) OPTIONAL MATCH (t)-[r:BLOCKS]->(blocked:Task) RETURN t.id AS id, t.title AS title, t.createdAt AS createdAt, collect(blocked.title) AS blocks

nodes.label: Prioritization Prompt
nodes.template:
You are a Decision Orchestrator. You will receive a JSON dataset of tasks from a Neo4j knowledge graph.

Phase 1 — Semantic Analysis:
Examine each task's title. Identify which tasks are inherently foundational, urgent, or high-impact based on their nature (e.g. infrastructure tasks before feature tasks, blocking items before dependent items).

Phase 2 — Constraint Analysis:
The 'blocks' array for each task lists tasks that CANNOT start until this task is complete. This is an absolute rule — a task that blocks others must always rank higher than every task it blocks.

Phase 3 — Synthesis:
Produce a final master ranked list. Tasks with no relationships ('orphans') should be inserted by semantic importance relative to graph-linked tasks.

Return ONLY a valid JSON array (no markdown, no explanation outside the JSON). Each element:
{
  "taskId": "<the task id>",
  "finalRank": <1 = highest priority>,
  "reasoning": "<one sentence explaining this rank>"
}

Task data:
{{input}}

config.llm_openai.system: You are a precise task prioritization engine. Always return valid JSON arrays only.

nodes.label: Neo4j — Write Priority Scores
nodes.query: UNWIND $rankings AS r MATCH (t:Task {id: r.taskId}) SET t.priority = r.finalRank, t.reasoning = r.reasoning
